simple.meaning: עוּל (ʻûwl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to suckle , i.e. give milk.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Genesis, 1 Samuel, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Genesis 33:13. The surrounding contexts include flock.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עוּל (H5763) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עוּל (ʻûwl) / H5763 is traced through Genesis 33:13, 1 Samuel 6:7, 1 Samuel 6:10, Psalms 78:71 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

timeline.evidenceText: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.
“Now therefore take and prepare yourselves a new cart and two milk cows on which there has come no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;
The men did so, and took two milk cows and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
from following the ewes that have their young,
